turn_text: congressman rose when you first got to washington what were some of the things that you you learn right away that maybe we're a little bit surprising to you
well

uh... you know the founders just trusted big government the central government they they uh... didn't like the idea having just read themselves from what they felt like was the tyranny of british rule and so when they set up our constitution that we work under today. They created a system of checks and balances that most of us are familiar with, three branches of government within the legislative branch that I serve in, two houses of Congress. They wanted to make it difficult for the federal government to do things because they wanted the federal government to be contemplative and they really wanted the state governments to be laboratories for democracy. They wanted most of the action to be happening at the state level. And so when I got to Washington, I realized two things. Number one is the magnificent plan that the founders have or had back then, I think, is still the best formula for our country. And number two, it's tough to get things done in Washington. There's a reason for the old adage is that we hear often of it will take an act of Congress, something we all say when something is going to be really difficult. And that's the way they wanted it. So it takes a lot to get things done in Washington. Sometimes that's very frustrating, particularly to those back at home that want to see government solve problems more quickly. But the founders, I think, had it right. We don't want our government kind of whipsawing back and forth from one solution to another. Unfortunately, we've seen the executive branch, the president that is, exerting, I think, too much power in recent years. And that's been true on both sides of the aisle, Republican and Democrat. I think we need to get back to the original vision that the founders have, where the states are where most things happen and where the federal government moves slowly and very deliberately to do what it should. And that means we've got to claw back power for the states. And we've also got to as members of congress uh... as an institution we've got the call back power from the executive branch branch that's been feeding it over the years
